milestones.title: Phase 1 — Source research
milestones.description: Confirm sources, reuse rights, identifiers, coverage and bounded integration plans before coding.

milestones.title: Phase 2 — Oregon healthcare access
milestones.description: Map verified public facility locations and shortage areas; search and data-quality checks.

milestones.title: Phase 3 — Local health exploration
milestones.description: Add tract-level estimates and boundaries with explicit uncertainty and geographic joins.

milestones.title: Phase 4 — Service-area analysis
milestones.description: Define and compare areas using defensible summaries; separate community need from commercial demand.

milestones.title: Phase 5 — National expansion
milestones.description: Generalize region configuration and validate scalable, reproducible multi-state workflows.

issues.title: Evaluate CMS public facility datasets
acceptance: Compare CMS facility datasets for coverage, reuse rights, update schedules and documented service fields.
Recommend hospitals as a bounded first target; record identifier semantics (CMS IDs versus NPIs), missing locations and API constraints.
Save source links and an evidence-based recommendation under docs/data-sources/.
issues.validation: A reviewer can follow the official links and reproduce representative read-only queries.

issues.title: Evaluate HRSA shortage designations and health-center data
acceptance: Identify authoritative downloads/APIs, licenses and update dates for HPSAs and health-center sites.
Distinguish geographic, population and facility designations; retain discipline and active status.
Document geographic identifiers, geometry availability and which claims the data cannot support.
issues.validation: Review sample Oregon records and document a defensible join and map strategy.

issues.title: Evaluate tract-level PLACES and Census geography
acceptance: Confirm Oregon tract estimates, available conditions/years, suppression and uncertainty fields.
Identify compatible tract boundary vintages and 11-digit GEOIDs.
Document why ZCTAs, postal ZIP codes and census tracts cannot be treated interchangeably.
issues.validation: Reproduce a sample county-to-tract join and record coverage/size estimates without changing the app.

issues.title: Define the expansion source catalog and data contracts
acceptance: Specify source URL, reuse rights, geography, identifiers, periods, update frequency and fetched-at metadata.
Define missing-value, uncertainty and geographic-join rules with small fixture examples.
Record needs-versus-demand limits: prevalence is not patient-level diagnosis, service capacity or purchase intent.
issues.validation: Review the contract against existing CDC/Census imports and candidate facility sources.

issues.title: Import and validate Oregon hospitals
acceptance: Implement bounded, cached imports for the recommended hospital dataset with retained provenance.
Deduplicate stable facility IDs and validate Oregon geography; retain unresolved locations without inventing facility coordinates.
Preserve prior snapshots on failures and add fixtures for duplicates, missing fields and changed records.
issues.validation: Run focused import/query tests and a documented live coverage check; no live-network dependency in CI.

issues.title: Import Oregon shortage designations
acceptance: Preserve designation ID, type, discipline, status, geography and source dates.
Use authoritative geometries/joins without collapsing unlike designations into one score.
Cache validated imports and retain old snapshots during failures.
issues.validation: Check known Oregon examples and test inactive designations, missing geometry and duplicates.

issues.title: Add facility and shortage-area map layers
acceptance: Add independent toggles with legends and accessible facility/area detail alternatives.
Show only validated coordinates and label unresolved-location coverage.
Keep health prevalence separate from shortage designations and facility supply; retain attribution.
issues.validation: Verify layer controls, picking/details, mobile behavior and absence of map API key requirements unless separately justified.

issues.title: Add facility search and public detail views
acceptance: Search public facility names and supported location/type fields.
Display only services/attributes actually reported by the selected source with dates and missing-value labels.
Link facility locations to surrounding community context without claiming it describes facility patients.
issues.validation: Test search filters, empty results, stable facility IDs and safe public-data exports.

issues.title: Report facility and shortage-data coverage
acceptance: Report duplicates, missing/invalid coordinates, source age and unresolved joins.
Distinguish absent values, unsupported fields and unavailable sources.
Add repeatable checks and documentation for reviewers.
issues.validation: Use fixtures covering each failure mode and confirm the report never treats missing supply as zero facilities.

issues.title: Import Oregon tract health estimates
acceptance: Implement documented bounded pagination and validated 11-digit tract IDs.
Preserve measure definitions, estimate years, intervals and unavailable values.
Keep county and tract estimates in distinct query paths and retain old snapshots on failure.
issues.validation: Test pagination boundaries, duplicate/suppressed rows, source failures and representative Oregon coverage.

issues.title: Add compatible Oregon tract boundaries
acceptance: Bundle or cache licensed boundaries with explicit vintage and provenance.
Validate tract GEOIDs and county prefixes; report missing joins and changed boundaries.
Document generalization and avoid representing ZIP polygons as tracts.
issues.validation: Check a sample county visually and test geometry/GEOID coverage against the selected release.

issues.title: Build state-to-county-to-tract navigation
acceptance: Offer map and keyboard-accessible drill-down with persistent geography selection.
Label geography, source period, missing records and uncertainty at each level.
Preserve shareable links and usable mobile performance.
issues.validation: Browser-test drill-down, links, unsupported locations and mobile layout.

issues.title: Document and expose small-area interpretation limits
acceptance: Explain modeled estimates, uncertainty, age composition and geographic changes in context.
Avoid treating tract estimates as individual diagnoses or summing prevalence rates.
Add clear unavailable/suppressed-state examples and a source-methodology reference.
issues.validation: Review scenarios with missing data and unlike periods; verify labels/exports retain definitions.

issues.title: Define reproducible service areas
acceptance: Start with explicit sets of counties or tracts and stable geography IDs.
Persist/share selected boundaries and document inclusion rules, overlaps and edge effects.
Exclude private patient/client addresses and defer drive-time APIs until their need and access are approved.
issues.validation: Round-trip saved areas and test duplicates, overlaps, empty areas and changed boundaries.

issues.title: Build defensible service-area summaries
acceptance: Count validated public facility locations with deduplication and source dates.
Aggregate demographic quantities only across compatible, non-overlapping areas with documented uncertainty limits.
Do not average/sum health prevalence or invent combined intervals when needed denominators/covariance are unavailable.
issues.validation: Use known fixtures and negative cases to prove unsupported aggregations are refused or clearly omitted.

issues.title: Compare and export service-area context
acceptance: Compare selected areas with units, periods, source references and missing-value status.
Label facility locations as supply indicators, not verified capacity or utilization.
Keep community need separate from commercial demand; no opaque opportunity score.
issues.validation: Verify reproducible comparisons, share links, CSVs, and mismatched-period/coverage warnings.

issues.title: Replace Oregon assumptions with region configuration
acceptance: Parameterize state FIPS, expected geography, source coverage and map bounds.
Migrate existing links/caches safely while preserving Oregon behavior.
Prepare Oregon and one additional state as representative targets.
issues.validation: Run region fixtures and Oregon regressions; verify no hardcoded 36-county assumption leaks across states.

issues.title: Scale storage and source refreshes across states
acceptance: Define measured resource budgets, partition/cache strategy and bounded downloads.
Use shared request limits appropriate to deployment replicas and safe concurrent snapshot replacement.
Keep representative development setup small and reproducible.
issues.validation: Measure cold/warm loads, memory and failure recovery on two states before broad rollout.

issues.title: Validate multi-state coverage and contributor workflow
acceptance: Verify authoritative sources/periods, joins and missingness in two states.
Document contributor setup and required checks with small non-secret CI fixtures.
Record remaining regional limitations rather than claiming nationwide completeness.
issues.validation: Complete a reproducible release checklist covering data, maps, links, exports, source outages and mobile use.
